questions: What is the exact definition of coprime positive integers P and Q when expressing a rational number x as P/Q?
How should the function f(x) handle the case when x is already an integer (i.e., when Q=1)?
What constitutes a "good sequence" when N=1, given that the constraint involves A_i for 1≤i≤N-1?
Should the gcd condition gcd(S₁,S₂,…,S_N)=1 be interpreted as requiring the overall gcd of all elements to be exactly 1, or at least 1?
What is the expected behavior when A_i=1 for some i, since this would require S_i/S_{i+1}=1 and thus S_i=S_{i+1}?
How should ties or equivalent sequences be handled in the scoring - are identical sequences with different indices counted separately?
What is the precise input format regarding whitespace and line separation for the integer N and sequence A?
Are there any additional constraints on the values of S_i beyond being positive integers that satisfy the given conditions?
answers: gcd(P,Q)=1, the standard definition of coprime.
If x is an integer, express it as x/1.
Not applicable; N is guaranteed to be at least 2.
gcd(S_1,...,S_N)=1 means the overall gcd is exactly 1, the standard definition.
Not applicable; sequences are tuples, so each distinct sequence contributes its score once.
The input format is fixed as two lines: the first line contains N, the second line contains the N-1 integers A_1,...,A_{N-1}, space-separated.
Not specified beyond being positive integers satisfying the stated equations and gcd condition.

For a positive rational number x, define f(x) as follows:
Express x as $\dfrac{P}{Q}$ using coprime positive integers P and Q, where gcd(P,Q)=1, the standard definition of coprime. f(x) is defined as the value P\times Q.
You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_{N-1}) of positive integers of length N-1.
We call a sequence S=(S_1,S_2,\dots,S_N) of positive integers of length N a good sequence if it satisfies all of the following conditions:
- For every integer i with 1\leq i\leq N-1, it holds that f\left(\dfrac{S_i}{S_{i+1}}\right)=A_i.
- $\gcd(S_1,S_2,\dots,S_N)=1$.
Define the score of a sequence as the product of all its elements.
Find the sum, modulo 998244353, of the scores of all good sequences.

Output

- 1\leq A_i\leq 1000 (1\leq i\leq N-1)
- All input values are integers.
